judgements.justification: Neither area chair moved away from its scores. B's meta-review only restates them ('a well-received paper by all the reviewers'). A's area chair gave its own reading, but that reading ends at the poster that A's 7, 7, 8 support.

No recommendation rests on a forecast beyond example-based RL. B's two-sentence meta-review makes no forecast. Reviewer forecasts stay within the paper's setting ('opens avenues for future work in this area'), and A's area chair limited 'rather significant impact' to 'some domains'.

The response moved scores in both committees, so neither stayed unchanged. A's Reviewer_yauQ raised to 7 'after reading the response and other reviewers' feedback'. B's Reviewer_9r4w raised to 8 because 'most concerns about this paper have been well addressed'.

B's top score came from a thin review. Reviewer_xycR's 9, the only 9 among the seven reviews, rests on a 2-hour, one-paragraph review with 'one minor comment'. Reviewer_LgSM's 8 rests on general praise and a raise that names no specific point. The careful reviews are close (A: 7, 7; B: 7, 8). A's one thin review, Reviewer_FCFz's, gave 8.

Only A raised the simple image tasks and the claims with no linked experiment. Both points are correct, and the paper concedes the image limitation in Sec. 6. These doubts held A's Reviewer_3uQ8 at 7 after the rebuttal, while B's reviewers praised the experiments as 'comprehensive' and 'extensive'.

Both committees saw that the work builds on prior ideas: A's Reviewer_yauQ named C-learning, and B's Reviewer_6QWr called the rationale 'not necessarily novel'. A's area chair read the paper as 'a mix of existing and new tools'. In B, Reviewer_6QWr still called the work 'very high quality', and B's area chair named no weakness.

No raise came from other reviewers alone. B's Reviewer_LgSM credits 'the other reviews and the authors' responses to them', and A's Reviewer_yauQ credits 'the response and other reviewers' feedback'. No reviewer posted in either visible discussion.

No rating clearly contradicts its text in the direction of the split. Reviewer_xycR's 9 fits its wholly positive text, which lacks only specifics (R04). Reviewer_6QWr's 7 sits below its 'very high quality' praise, but the review also calls the rationale 'not necessarily novel', and a lower B score narrows the gap.
No reviewer gave a borderline score. Every rating is 7 or higher, and the least confident reviewer, B's Reviewer_9r4w (confidence 3, math not checked), rated 8.

reasoning: Stage 1 finds that B's oral came from its higher scores. B did not find more in the paper. Neither area chair moved away from its scores (R01 no). B's only 9 came from a one-paragraph review, and Reviewer_LgSM's 8 from a generic one (R04). Only A raised the simple image tasks and the unlinked claims, which held Reviewer_3uQ8 at 7 (R05). Both committees saw the ties to prior work, and A gave them more weight (R06). The response moved scores in both committees (R03 no). Each raise that credits other reviewers also credits the response (R07 no). I added no reason. The 9 from a thin review fits R04 with a plain reading, as single thin high scores did in turns 1 and 3. B's two-sentence meta-review only passed its scores through. A's area chair also ended where its scores pointed, so neither area chair caused the split. The rebuttal answered Reviewer_yauQ's wrong baseline count and Reviewer_3uQ8's wrong reading of sawyer_push. Nothing shows that either error set a final score.
